data.name: Kaunteyas
data.gender_notes: Kaunteyas is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kaunteyas is a name for a child born from Kunti, the mother of the Pandavas in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. The name Kaunteyas carries the meaning “Descendant of Kunti” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kaunteyas usually hope their child will grow to embody descendant of kunti and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kaunteyas belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Descendant of Kunti.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kaunteyas total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Kaunteyas or the descendants of Kunti hold a significant place in Indian mythology and culture, especially in the Mahabharata epic where they are represented by the five Pandava brothers - Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva. The name has been passed down through generations and is still prevalent among Hindus as a proud familial or personal identity. It has also been referenced in various art forms such as literature, music, theater, and visual arts.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the Kaunteyas are considered an embodiment of righteousness, unity, and resilience. The story of the Pandavas, who faced numerous trials and tribulations before finally emerging victorious, inspires Hindus to persevere through life's challenges and maintain dharma (righteousness) even in the face of adversity. The name Kaunteyas also holds the blessings of their mother, Kunti, who is revered as a devoted and virtuous woman in Hindu mythology. Thus, holding a Kaunteyas name symbolizes the spiritual qualities of inner strength, perseverance, and righteousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The Kaunteyas are descendants of Shruti-rishi Kaundinya, who attained enlightenment through the recitation of the Vedas. Their name signifies deep reverence for sacred knowledge and the spiritual journey towards self-realization.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the name of Kunti, mother of the Pandavas.

historical_references.reference: The Kaunteyas were a great clan of the Mahabharata period in ancient India, with Kurukshetra as their capital and Kunti as their queen, from whom they derived their name. They were the maternal uncles and protectors of the Pandava brothers, and played a significant role in the Mahabharata war.

The Kaunteyas were also known as the Panchalas, and were a powerful tribe inhabiting the region of modern Gujarat in ancient India. They were ruled by King Prthu, who was the first King of the Solar Dynasty, and they played a major role in the early history of India, particularly in the establishment of the first agrarian civilization.
